decision.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its target interest rate in a range of 1-3/4 to 2 percent while announcing technical measures to support effective monetary policy implementation.

changes.explanation: The statement focuses on technical monetary policy implementation details rather than standard policy adjustments.

changes.quote: Consistent with its January 2019 Statement Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation and Balance Sheet Normalization, the Committee reaffirms its intention to implement monetary policy in a regime in which an ample supply of reserves ensures that control over the level of the federal funds rate and other short-term interest rates is exercised primarily through the setting of the Federal Reserve's administered rates, and in which active management of the supply of reserves is not required.
changes.explanation: The Fed reaffirmed its framework of maintaining an ample supply of reserves so that short-term rates are controlled primarily through administered rates.

changes.quote: In light of recent and expected increases in the Federal Reserve's non-reserve liabilities, the Federal Reserve will purchase Treasury bills at least into the second quarter of next year in order to maintain over time ample reserve balances at or above the level that prevailed in early September 2019.
changes.explanation: The Fed plans to purchase Treasury bills to maintain adequate reserve levels following increases in non-reserve liabilities.

changes.quote: In addition, the Federal Reserve will conduct term and overnight repurchase agreement operations at least through January of next year to ensure that the supply of reserves remains ample even during periods of sharp increases in non-reserve liabilities, and to mitigate the risk of money market pressures that could adversely affect policy implementation.
changes.explanation: Repo operations will be conducted to keep reserves ample and prevent money market pressures.

changes.quote: These actions are purely technical measures to support the effective implementation of the FOMC's monetary policy, and do not represent a change in the stance of monetary policy.
changes.explanation: The central bank emphasized that these operations are technical adjustments and do not change the overall monetary policy stance.

tone_quotes.quote: These actions are purely technical measures to support the effective implementation of the FOMC's monetary policy, and do not represent a change in the stance of monetary policy.
The Committee will continue to monitor money market developments as it assesses the level of reserves most consistent with efficient and effective policy implementation.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 15.13% APR costs about $63.04 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.76% and moved +9 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.65% would rise by about $15.27 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 3.5%, and employers added an average of 176k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.7% over the past year (September 2019); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 4.8% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +10 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 1.09%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.39% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that upcoming meetings will focus on technical balance sheet management and reserve levels alongside traditional policy.

citations.detail: Effective October 15, 2019, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 1-3/4 to 2 percent.
